items.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: I just heard Charles Tollver’s big band.

ctx.x: Yeah. It’s a sort of a different way of codifying it, it might not have been four bars later that you decided to come in with that.

But that’s what I mean, you apply yourself to the situation and so therefore what the definition, how you define time, is different than how you define time in a twelve bar blues. This might be longer or shorter than a twelve bar blues, depending on where you start on it, but it’s still time. It is that time. I just heard Charles Tollver’s big band. And he does this thing, a phrase, it’s a phrase. But in that phrase he has elements. He has the saxophones going [scats] and he has the trumpets going [scats] and he…

practice rooms you know? I said but these are the same notes I play when I do the Haydn Trumpet Concerto, why can’t I play like a bebop, so what’s the difference? “You can’t play that in the practice room, you have to get out of the practice room if you’re going to play that.”
